grf.hypothesis: Build-local untracked dependency files can make a checkout-level git status dirty even though they are not part of the committed source authority and do not contaminate a fresh exact-head staged repository.
grf.strongest_counterhypothesis: Untracked build-local files may still leak into staging or hide a real source mutation, so ignoring them at the outer checkout could weaken provenance.
grf.discriminator: Create a disposable committed Git repository, add an untracked Vercel-like node_modules decoy, compare status with untracked-files=all versus untracked-files=no, then fetch the exact HEAD into a fresh shallow staging repository and require full cleanliness including untracked files.

bounded_unusual_experiment.name: VERCEL_BUILD_LOCAL_UNTRACKED_CONTAMINATION_DECOY
bounded_unusual_experiment.interpretation: Checkout-level untracked dependency dirt is not sufficient evidence that committed source authority is dirty; full cleanliness belongs on the freshly materialized exact-head staging repository. This does not validate PR #765 or EntityOS itself.
bounded_unusual_experiment.rollback: Temporary repository removed automatically; no product/runtime state changed.
